meetings.route: Visitor permit with a special business endorsement (extra AUD 100, up to 30 days)
meetings.detail: Tuvalu's Immigration Regulations bar employment and business on a plain visitor permit. Business activities explicitly include attending a conference or training session, performing professional services (including for the Government and NGOs) and exploratory negotiations. A visitor permit endorsed for business is available on arrival for an extra fee.
meetings.next: Ask for the business endorsement on arrival, or confirm in advance with the Principal Immigration Officer.

volunteering.next: Ask Tuvalu Immigration in writing before travel.

visa-preparation.entry_summary: Visitor permit on arrival, up to 30 days; AUD 100 unless your nationality is on the fee-exemption list.

steps.step: Arrive with a passport valid 6 months, an onward or return ticket, accommodation and enough money; the permit is issued on arrival.

steps: The permit doesn't allow work, business, study or proselytising; you can't have spent more than 3 months in Tuvalu in the past 12.
visa-preparation.recheck_note: Whether Australia is on the fee-exemption schedule wasn't confirmed.

laws.rule: It is illegal to import, export, cultivate or distribute drugs. Penalties include fines and imprisonment.
laws.heading: Illegal drugs and prison sentences

laws.rule: Homosexuality is illegal in Tuvalu. If you’re found guilty of consensual sex between adult males, you could face up to 14 years in prison. Read more advice for LGBT+ travellers .
laws.heading: LGBT+ travellers

laws.rule: There is one local mobile network in Tuvalu, other international networks will not work. You can buy local SIM cards in Funafuti.
laws.heading: Internet and phone services

laws.rule: There are no ATMs in Tuvalu, and credit or debit card payments are not accepted. Bring enough Australian dollars in cash with you for the duration of your trip.
laws.heading: Money
